mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW X3 xDrive30e engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A B48B20 plug-in hybrid engine for the BMW X3 xDrive30e typically costs £2,500-£5,800 supply-only depending on condition - used hybrid units start around £2,500, reconditioned from £3,500, and fully rebuilt from £4,500. Supply & fit adds £600-£1,000 due to hybrid system complexity.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW X3 xDrive30e B48B20 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the B48B20 is generally regarded as a reliable and refined engine when properly maintained. It avoids the major timing chain issues of the N20, but coolant system failures and oil leaks are well-documented weak points. The hybrid system is generally reliable, though battery degradation is a long-term consideration.

mainEntity.name: What causes coolant loss on the BMW X3 xDrive30e B48B20 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B48B20's plastic coolant components - water pump, thermostat housing, and coolant transfer pipe - become brittle under thermal cycling, developing cracks that cause coolant loss. This is the most common failure point on B48 engines.

mainEntity.name: What is the electric range of the BMW X3 xDrive30e and how does it affect engine replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW X3 xDrive30e offers up to 30 miles of electric-only range on a full charge. When replacing the petrol engine, the hybrid system must be recalibrated and the high-voltage battery tested to ensure proper integration. This adds complexity and cost compared to a conventional engine replacement.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a BMW X3 xDrive30e?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 2019-2024 BMW X3 xDrive30e is typically worth £20,000-£35,000. A rebuilt B48B20 hybrid engine at £3,500-£5,800 is a sound investment if the car is otherwise in good condition. The xDrive30e's strong residual values make engine replacement economically viable.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used engine in my BMW X3 xDrive30e and will it match my hybrid system?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can fit a used engine in your BMW X3 xDrive30e, but the engine code (B48B20) must match exactly, and the hybrid system must be recalibrated. The high-voltage battery and electric motor must also be tested for compatibility with the replacement petrol unit. Used engines from non-hybrid B48 applications may not be compatible.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a reconditioned and used BMW X3 xDrive30e engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned BMW X3 xDrive30e engine is fully stripped, machined, and rebuilt with new wear parts, and the hybrid system is fully tested and recalibrated. A used engine is removed from a donor vehicle with unknown internal and hybrid system condition. Reconditioned units include warranty and address known failure points; used engines offer lower upfront cost but higher risk.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW X3 xDrive30e (G01) - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The xDrive30e joined the G01 X3 range in 2019 as BMW's first plug-in hybrid variant of its popular mid-size SUV. Combining a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine with an electric motor and high-voltage battery, the xDrive30e delivered a compelling blend of performance, efficiency, and lower benefit-in-kind tax for company car drivers. Built on BMW's CLAR platform, the xDrive30e shared its powertrain architecture with the 330e and 530e, making it a proven and well-developed PHEV system.

milestones.description: xDrive30e introduced to UK market with B48B20 2.0L four-cylinder turbo petrol engine (184hp), 80kW electric motor, 12.0 kWh battery, combined 292hp, eight-speed Steptronic automatic, xDrive all-wheel drive
Minor software updates to improve electric range and charging performance
G01 LCI (facelift) brings styling updates; xDrive30e continues with revised battery management
G01 production ends; G45 generation replaces it with updated PHEV system

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW X3 xDrive30e is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points specific to the B48B20 plug-in hybrid powertrain.

commonProblems.h2: BMW X3 xDrive30e (G01) - What It Costs to Fix, and When Replacement Makes Sense
commonProblems.h3: The BMW X3 xDrive30e's plug-in hybrid powertrain combines the B48B20 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol engine with an 80kW electric motor and 12.0 kWh battery pack. While the B48 petrol unit is generally reliable and significantly improved over the N20 it replaced, it shares known issues with the wider B48 family - coolant system failures, oil leaks, and timing chain tensioner wear. However, the hybrid system introduces additional complexity: high-voltage battery degradation, charging system issues, and electric motor bearing wear are the primary concerns as these vehicles age out of warranty. Every rebuilt B48B20 engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded cooling system components and full hybrid system integration testing, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: B48B20 Coolant System Failure - Why Your BMW X3 xDrive30e Loses Coolant and Overheats
problems.rootCause: The B48 engine's plastic coolant components - including the water pump, thermostat housing, and coolant transfer pipe - become brittle under thermal cycling. Cracks develop, causing coolant loss that can lead to sudden overheating and head gasket failure. This is the most common B48 failure point.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, thermostat housing, coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; prevents overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace coolant transfer pipe, bleed system

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete B48 unit with upgraded cooling components, hybrid system integration testing, and 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if overheating has warped cylinder head.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2019-2024 BMW X3 xDrive30e is valued at approximately £20,000-£35,000 depending on mileage, condition and trim. At this value band, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine (£3,500-£5,800) is a sound investment if the car is otherwise in good condition. The xDrive30e's strong residual values make engine replacement economically viable.
problems.recommendation: B48 coolant leaks are the single most discussed issue on X3 forums. If you smell coolant or see the low coolant warning, act immediately. Check your coolant level monthly. A £450-£800 specialist repair is far cheaper than a £3,500-£5,800 engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B48B20 BMW X3 xDrive30e engine prices

problems.h4: B48B20 Oil Leaks - Valve Cover and Oil Filter Housing Gaskets
problems.rootCause: The oil filter housing gasket and valve cover gasket degrade over time, causing oil leaks. The oil filter housing on B48 engines is particularly problematic - the plastic housing can crack, leading to oil leaks externally or internally.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gasket, clean oil residue
repairOptions.longevity: Resolves external oil leaks; prevents oil dripping onto exhaust.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil filter housing gasket, oil change
repairOptions.longevity: Resolves oil leaks from filter housing.

problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the B48 are common but not catastrophic if addressed early. A small oil leak around the valve cover or oil filter housing is a relatively inexpensive fix at a specialist. However, if left unchecked, oil can drip onto the exhaust or turbocharger, creating a fire risk - address oil leaks promptly.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for BMW X3 xDrive30e B48B20 oil leak repair

problems.group: BMW X3 xDrive30e High-Voltage Battery Degradation
problems.h4: BMW X3 xDrive30e High-Voltage Battery Degradation - The Hidden Cost of PHEV Ownership
problems.rootCause: The 12.0 kWh lithium-ion battery pack loses capacity over time, reducing electric-only range and potentially causing hybrid system fault codes. Temperature extremes and frequent rapid charging accelerate degradation. BMW identified isolated cases of impurities in battery cell production affecting some 2020-2021 models.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace degraded cells, rebalance battery management system
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if only a few cells are degraded.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace entire 12.0 kWh battery pack with factory-spec unit
repairOptions.longevity: Required if battery is beyond reconditioning or has failed completely.

problems.recommendation: If your BMW X3 xDrive30e's electric range has dropped significantly or you see hybrid system warnings, have the battery health checked by a specialist. Battery reconditioning is often more cost-effective than full replacement. However, if the battery has failed completely, replacement is the only option.
problems.cta: -> Enquire about BMW X3 xDrive30e hybrid battery inspection and replacement

problems.h4: B48B20 Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Rattling on Start-Up
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, causing chain slack and a metallic rattle on cold start. While far less common than on the N20, poor maintenance and extended oil change intervals can accelerate wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tensioner, inspect chain and guides
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early and no chain damage.
Recommended if rattle is persistent or chain has stretched.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete B48 unit with upgraded timing components, hybrid system integration testing, and 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped timing or caused valve damage.

problems.recommendation: The B48B20 timing chain is far more reliable than the N20 - most owners will never need to replace it. However, if you hear a rattling noise on cold start or the engine is approaching 100,000 miles with no chain service history, a specialist inspection is recommended. Regular oil changes every 8,000-10,000 miles are critical for chain longevity.
